## Day 1 Theme

Solar work starts with orientation, shared language, safe habits, and verification. The goal is not to overload students with math. The goal is to make the room safe enough to learn and practical enough to matter.

## Learning Targets

- Explain what PV means and why solar work starts with observation, labels, and safe habits.
- Name the basic parts of a small PV system: solar module, charge controller, battery, fuse, load, and inverter.
- Describe the class rule: measure and verify before trusting a label.
- Practice group roles, cleanup expectations, and first-day classroom agreements.
- Connect Day 1 to the Cohort 6 RV solar capstone.

## Core Diagram

Sun -> Solar Module -> Charge Controller -> Battery -> Fuse Panel -> DC Loads
Battery -> Inverter -> AC Loads

## Full Day Flow

- 10:00-10:15 | Arrival, names, room reset | Students settle in, instructor checks energy level, materials out.
- 10:15-10:35 | Welcome to PV101 | What PV means, why this class matters, and how the RV capstone fits.
- 10:35-11:00 | Class agreements | Safety, respect, asking for help, no public shaming, cleanup is part of the job.
- 11:00-11:20 | What is a solar system? | Module -> charge controller -> battery -> fuse/load -> inverter when needed.
- 11:20-11:30 | Break | Reset, water, bathroom.
- 11:30-12:05 | Solar scavenger hunt | Groups identify parts from pictures or physical examples.
- 12:05-12:30 | RV capstone preview | What in an RV needs power? Students list loads and questions.
- 12:30-1:00 | Lunch | No work during lunch unless students choose to keep discussing.
- 1:00-1:35 | Labels vs verification | Why labels help but do not replace testing and tracing.
- 1:35-2:10 | Group build: system map | Students draw the energy path for a simple RV solar system.
- 2:10-2:30 | Quiz | Short low-pressure check for teaching quality and vocabulary.
- 2:30-2:50 | Exit ticket | What makes sense, what is confusing, what students want to learn.
- 2:50-3:00 | Cleanup and preview Day 2 | Meter readiness and electricity basics tomorrow.

## Cohort 6 Future Fix

For future Day 1 and Day 2 materials, assume the default classroom battery is a 12.8V LiFePO4 battery unless Tim says other batteries are available. Do not assume AA, AAA, or 9V batteries are ready for classroom use.
